newsitem.title: JORDAN: Egypt's Mubarak cautious over Netanyahu meeting.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak cautious over Netanyahu meeting.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak struck a note of caution on Saturday ahead of a summit next week with Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu aimed at breaking an impasse in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.

"I cannot guarantee our effort will succeed 100 percent... the circumstances have got very tough," Mubarak told a news conference with King Hussein in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba after brief one-day talks to coordinate positions.
Mubarak and Netanyahu are expected to meet in the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh on Tuesday.

Egypt, partner to a 1979 treaty with Israel, hopes to break the Israel-PLO peacemaking deadlock that has existed since March when Israel began building a controversial Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel since 1967.
The Palestinians say talks can resume only after Israel stops work on the settlement. Egypt, which considers itself an unofficial sponsor of the peace talks, supports their position.
Mubarak said his senior adviser Osama el-Baz would return to Israel on Sunday for a second round of talks to prepare for Tuesday's summit.
"Dr Baz will continue tomorrow (Sunday) at the request of Israel the discussions which hopefully will arrive at moving the process, and a solution which is a just one," Mubarak said.
Mubarak said there was an urgent need to break the impasse but said it was too early to talk of an Egyptian initiative to re-activate Palestinian self-rule talks.

"We still cannot talk about initiatives until we see the Israeli side, what idea they have, and examine it and then present it to the Palestinian side and if there is agreement, to enter into negotiations," he added.
Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Mousa said on Friday the summit would succeed if Israel agreed to stop building settlements for Jews on land captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
Asked if there were any preconditions for the summit Mubarak said: "We have not talked about conditions, we are talking about how to solve the present crisis, we cannot say preconditions."

King Hussein, who used his close ties with both Israel and the Palestinians to broker a January deal on an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron, said his country supported Egyptian efforts to restart the stalled talks.
"We bless all the efforts our Egyptian brothers have taken and support them," the monarch said.
But Mubarak warned against a delay in resuming peace talks and said both Netanyahu and King Hussein agreed with him on the need to act quickly to spare the region instability.

"If the situation continues as it is now, the consequences of it will not be good at all...I hope with all my heart that we will succeed. We should not despair and if despair engulfs our hearts there will be no peace," Mubarak said.
"I believe the prime minister of Israel, I and his majesty the king are agreed that the position now towards the peace process requires a move in any way," he added.
